title: AI Coding Toolkit Implementation Dataflow
description: impl-dataflow is shorthand for implementation dataflow. This JSON models how a feature or system's behavior is realized by implementation entities: classes and modules with their functions, mutable instance state, interface and external components, static data, and direct data transfers, state accesses, and ownership relationships. It represents proposed designs or implemented behavior, with diff hunks providing evidence during code review.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the Implementation Dataflow schema used by this document.

stage.description: The development stage represented by this dataflow: proposed implementation during high-level design or implemented behavior during code review.

diffHunks.description: Exact unified diff hunks referenced by implementation entities and relationships during code review.

changedClassCount.description: Derived number of added, modified, or deleted classes.

changedFunctionCount.description: Derived number of added, modified, or deleted functions in changed classes and modules.

changedComponentCount.description: Derived number of added, modified, or deleted UI, system input/output, and external dependency components.

changedDataflowRelationshipCount.description: Derived number of added, modified, or deleted dataflow relationships, including state reads and writes.

classes.description: Implementation classes represented by the document. Use an empty array when none are represented. Class, module, component, and static-data names must be unique across the document.

modules.description: Named implementation units containing functions that are not owned by classes. A unit may be a language-level module, namespace, package, or source file. Use an empty array when none are represented. Names must be unique across classes, modules, components, and static data.

components.description: UI surfaces, system inputs and outputs, and external dependencies at the implementation boundary. Use an empty array when none are represented.

staticData.description: Fixed data read by represented functions, such as constants or static lookup data. Use an empty array when none are represented. External files and storage remain external-dependency components.

relationships.description: Direct relationships between represented entities. Preserve intermediate participants. Use dataflow relationships for data transfers, class-owned state reads and writes, and external storage access. Relationships express dependencies and data movement, not execution order.

file.description: Repository-relative path to the changed file.

patch.description: Exact unified diff hunk, including the @@ header.

diffHunkIds.description: References to relevant diff hunks supporting this changed entry. Omit for unchanged entries and high-level designs.

changeType.description: How an entity or relationship differs from the existing architecture. Use added for a new entry, modified for a changed declaration, responsibility, contract, or relationship, deleted for a removed entry, and unchanged for an existing entry reused without such a change. Participation or a new connection alone does not modify an endpoint.

component.description: A UI surface, system input or output, or external dependency. Represent implementation handlers and adapters as class or module functions instead.

name.description: Unique across classes, modules, components, and static data; referenced by relationship endpoints.

description.description: What the component is or represents, including a URL, file path, storage key, or other concrete identifier when available.

oneOf.description: A UI surface that receives user input or presents output.
Data supplied to this system by another system or workflow. May only be the source of a dataflow.
A final result sent to another system or workflow. May only be the target of a dataflow.
An external service, file, datastore, or other I/O endpoint used by the implementation.

staticData.description: Fixed data that a represented function reads without updating. Its name is unique across classes, modules, components, and static data.

class.description: An implementation class represented by the document.

functions.description: Functions represented for this class. Function names must be unique within the class.

stateVariables.description: Mutable instance fields whose declaration or architectural meaning is added, modified, or deleted, plus unchanged mutable fields referenced by a dataflow relationship. Excludes static or class variables, local variables, unrelated fields, explicitly read-only fields, fields initialized at declaration or construction but never written afterward, and fields used only as references to owned child objects. Constructor assignment is initialization rather than a state update. Runtime writes do not by themselves make an existing field modified. State-variable names must be unique within the class.

variableExposure.description: Existing declarations exposed to this class's changes; null when the inventory is required but not yet known.

module.description: A named implementation unit that groups functions without a class owner, regardless of the source language's term for that unit.

functions.description: Functions represented for this unit that are not owned by a class. Function names must be unique within the unit.

function.description: An implementation function owned by a class or grouped in a module.

stateVariable.description: A mutable instance field represented for its class. Dataflow relationships reference the exact state-variable entry.

function.description: Existing function containing the parameter or local.

file.description: Canonical repository-relative path to the declaration in current code.

classEndpoint.description: References a class by its document-unique name.

functionEndpoint.description: References a function by name and its class or module owner.

stateVariableEndpoint.description: References a state variable by its class name and class-local state-variable name.

componentEndpoint.description: References a component by its document-unique name.

staticDataEndpoint.description: References fixed data by its document-unique name.

dataflowEndpoint.description: A class or module function, or component that directly sends or receives data.

oneOf.description: A direct data transfer between function or component endpoints, a read from static data by a function, or a mutable instance state access. A state variable as the source means a read by the target function; a state variable as the target means a write by the source function. System-input components may only be sources and system-output components may only be targets. Record request and response paths as separate relationships.
A class owns a child class. A field used only for this ownership is represented by composition rather than as a state variable.

relationship.description: A direct architectural relationship between two represented endpoints.

from.description: Explicit source reference, constrained by relationship type.

to.description: Explicit target reference, constrained by relationship type.

dataDescription.description: What data this relationship transfers, reads, or modifies.
